nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ مِن دَآبَّةٍ وَٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ﴾.
It has been said: the meaning is: and to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens of the angels, and whatever is in the earth of creatures that crawl (dābba), and the angels, i.e. the angels who are on the earth; and Allah knows best what He intended.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: everything that has a soul (rūḥ) is a dābba, prostrating to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱللَّهُ لاَ تَتَّخِذُواْ إِلـٰهَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾.
That is: do not worship anything besides Allah, even if you seek to draw near to Allah by worshipping it; and He brought «اثنين» (two) for emphasis (tawkīd).
It has also been said: the meaning is: do not take two [beings] as gods.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَهُ مَا فِي ٱلْسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَلَهُ ٱلدِّينُ وَاصِباً﴾.
ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: [«واصباً» means] obligatory.
It has also been said: obedience in every circumstance, even if there is «الوَصَب» in it, which is fatigue; and this is the meaning of the saying of al-Ḥasan.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: ﴿وَلَهُ ٱلدِّينُ وَاصِباً﴾ — he said: perpetual; do you not hear His saying ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ وَاصِبٌ﴾? That is: perpetual. Maymūn ibn Mihrān said the same.
Ibn Jurayj narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿وَلَهُ ٱلدِّينُ وَاصِباً﴾ — he said: sincere devotion (al-ikhlāṣ), and «الواصب» is the perpetual.
This is what is well known in the language; one says «وَصَبَ يَصِبُ وُصُوباً» when a thing lasts; and «الدِّين» is obedience. The meaning is that everyone who is obeyed, his being obeyed comes to an end through perishing or passing away, except Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَمَا بِكُم مِّن نِّعْمَةٍ فَمِنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is: whatever you have of abundance in provision or health in body is from Allah. ﴿ثُمَّ إِذَا مَسَّكُمُ ٱلضُّرُّ﴾ — which is affliction and hardship — ﴿فَإِلَيْهِ تَجْأَرُونَ﴾, i.e. you call out and cry for help.
One says «جَأَرَ، يَجْأَرُ، جُؤَاراً» when someone raises his voice crying for help, because of hunger or something else.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ ثُمَّ إِذَا كَشَفَ ٱلضُّرَّ عَنْكُمْ إِذَا فَرِيقٌ مِّنْكُم بِرَبِّهِمْ يُشْرِكُونَ، لِيَكْفُرُواْ بِمَآ آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾.
It has been said: the meaning is: so that they make the blessing a means to disbelief, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿رَبَّنَا لَيُضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلكَ﴾.
It has also been said: so that they deny the blessing which He bestowed upon them, as the poet said:
 * "والكفرُ مَخْبثَةٌ لنفسِ المُنْعِمِ" *
(And ingratitude is a cause of disgust to the soul of the benefactor.)

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿فَتَمَتَّعُواْ فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
This is by way of threat, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿فَمَنْ شَاءَ فَلْيُؤْمِنْ، وَمَنْ شَاءَ فَلْيَكْفُر﴾ — that is: We have sent the messengers, made things clear and warned; so whoever wishes, let him disbelieve after this, for the punishment will descend upon him.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِمَا لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ نَصِيباً مِّمّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ﴾.
He means: what they used to assign to their idols from their crops and their livestock, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿فَقَالُوا هَذَا لِلَّهِ بِزَعْمهِمْ، وَهَذَا لِشُرَكَائِنَا﴾.

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِلَّهِ ٱلْبَنَاتِ سُبْحَانَهُ وَلَهُمْ مَّا يَشْتَهُونََ﴾.
That is: and for themselves the sons.

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإِذَا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُمْ بِٱلأُنْثَىٰ ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدّاً﴾.
That is: he becomes dejected and grieved; the Arabs say this of everyone who is grieved and whose colour has changed from grief: "his face has turned black".
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ﴾ [verse 58].
«الكظيم» is the sorrowful one who hides his anger and does not complain of what afflicts him.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يَتَوَارَىٰ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ مِن سُوۤءِ مَا بُشِّرَ بِهِ﴾.
It is narrated that when a child was about to be born to one of them, he would hide himself at that time, or before it; if a male was born to him he was delighted with it, and if a female was born to him he concealed himself, and perhaps he buried her alive.
Then He made that clear by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أَيُمْسِكُهُ عَلَىٰ هُونٍ أَمْ يَدُسُّهُ فِي ٱلتُّرَابِ﴾.
Al-Jaḥdarī read ﴿أَمْ يَدُسُّهَا في التُّرَابِ﴾, referring it back to His saying "بالأنثى"; and that obliges him to read ﴿أَيمسكُهَا﴾.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read ﴿أيمسكُهُ عَلى هَوَانٍ﴾ and said: «هَوَان» and «هُون» are one and the same.
Al-Aʿmash read: ﴿أيمسكُهُ على سُوءٍ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayd related from al-Kisāʾī that he said: in the dialect of Quraysh «الهُوْن» and «الهَوَان» have one meaning; and he said: the dialect of Banū Tamīm makes «الهون» the maṣdar (verbal noun) of a thing that is easy (al-hayyin).
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَلاَ سَآءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ﴾.
Because they ascribed daughters to Allah while they themselves detest them with this detestation.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ مَثَلُ ٱلسَّوْءِ وَلِلَّهِ ٱلْمَثَلُ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda that he said: ﴿ٱلْمَثَلُ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ﴾ is: there is no god but Allah.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda that he said: ﴿ٱلْمَثَلُ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ﴾ is sincere devotion and the affirmation of Oneness (al-tawḥīd).
The two meanings are one, i.e. to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, belongs Oneness and the negation of every object of worship besides Him.

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ يُؤَاخِذُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّاسَ بِظُلْمِهِمْ مَّا تَرَكَ عَلَيْهَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ﴾ [verse 61].
That is: on the earth; it had not been mentioned, because the meaning was already understood.

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِلَّهِ مَا يَكْرَهُونَ﴾.
He means the daughters.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَتَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُهُمُ ٱلْكَذِبَ أَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ﴾.
Mujāhid said: it is their saying: "Ours are the sons."
Someone else said: «الحسنى» is Paradise.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لاَ جَرَمَ أَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلْنَّارَ وَأَنَّهُمْ مُّفْرَطُونَ﴾.
It has been said: «لا» is a rejection of their words, and «جَرَمَ» means: it has become necessary, it has become due.
Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already discussed it exhaustively.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَأَنَّهُمْ مُّفْرَطُونَ﴾.
This is how al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read it, with fatḥa on the rāʾ and without doubling.
They differed about its interpretation: al-Ḥasan said: ﴿مُفْرَطُونَ﴾ means hastened to the Fire.
Hushaym said: Abū Bishr and Ḥuṣayn informed us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: ﴿وَأَنَّهُمْ مُّفْرَطُونَ﴾ — he said: left behind and forgotten.
Ibn Jurayj narrated from Mujāhid that he said: ﴿مفرطون﴾: forgotten.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the saying of al-Ḥasan is better known and more familiar in the language.
The lexicographers related: he is «فَارِط» and «فَرَط» [i.e. one who goes ahead]; and in the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ: "I am your faraṭ at the Pool", i.e. the one who goes before you to it until you come down to me; and «أفرطته» is said when you have sent someone ahead. A number of the lexicographers recited:
فَاسْتَعْجَلُونا وكانُوا من صَحَابتِنَا * كَمَا تعجَّل فُرَّاطٌ لِوُرَّادِ
(They hastened ahead of us, though they were of our company, as forerunners hasten ahead of those coming down to the water.)
The view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid was held by "Abū ʿUbayda, al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ".
Abū Jaʿfar said: so according to the view of al-Ḥasan [it means] hastened and sent ahead to the Fire, and according to the view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid, left in the Fire.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās read ﴿وَأنَّهُمْ مُفْرِطُون﴾: going to excess in wrongdoing, as one says «فَرَطَ فلانٌ على فلانٍ» when he exceeds him and says to him more evil than the other said.
Abū Jaʿfar and al-Suddī read ﴿وأنَّهُم مُفَرِّطُونَ﴾, and its meaning is: neglectful, i.e. they were neglectful in this world.

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي ٱلأَنْعَامِ لَعِبْرَةً نُّسْقِيكُمْ مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ مِن بَيْنِ فَرْثٍ وَدَمٍ لَّبَناً خَالِصاً﴾ [verse 66].
«الفَرْث» is what is in the stomach (al-karish); one says «أفرثتُ الكرِشَ» when you have taken out what is in it. The meaning is that the food contains what is in the stomach, and from it comes the blood, then the milk comes out pure from the blood.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿سَآئِغاً لِلشَّارِبِينَ﴾.
That is: smooth, so that whoever drinks it does not choke on it.

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمِن ثَمَرَاتِ ٱلنَّخِيلِ وَٱلأَعْنَابِ تَتَّخِذُونَ مِنْهُ سَكَراً وَرِزْقاً حَسَناً﴾.
ʿAmr ibn Sufyān narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: «السَّكَر» is what is forbidden of their fruit, and the good provision is what is lawful of their fruit.
Shuʿba narrated from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm and al-Shaʿbī, that they both said: «السَّكَر» is what was forbidden, and it has been abrogated.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda that he said: «السَّكَر» is a nabīdh (fermented drink) of the non-Arabs, and it [the verse] has been abrogated.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that he said: «السَّكَر» has been forbidden.
Mujāhid said: «السَّكَر» is what has been forbidden of wine, and the good provision is what has been made lawful of dates and grapes.
Abū Jaʿfar said: it is more fitting that the verse be abrogated, because the prohibition of wine was in Medina, while [Sūrat] al-Naḥl is Meccan.
As for the narration from Ibn ʿAbbās, it is as if its meaning is that the verse is by way of informing that they do that, not that He permitted them to do so; and that is its meaning.
It is a narration that is weak on account of "ʿAmr ibn Sufyān".
Abū Jaʿfar said: there is another view about the meaning of «السَّكَر»: Abū ʿUbayda said: «السَّكَر» is food (al-ṭuʿm), and he recited:
 * "جَعَلْتَ عَيْبَ الأَكْرَمينَ سَكَرَا" *
(You made the faults of the noblest your "sakar".)
That is: you made disparaging them [your] food.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-Zajjāj said: this saying of Abū ʿUbayda is not known, and the exegetes hold the opposite of it; and he has no proof in the verse he recited, because its meaning, according to others, is that he is describing that she gets intoxicated (tatakhammar) with people's faults.

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَوْحَىٰ رَبُّكَ إِلَىٰ ٱلنَّحْلِ أَنِ ٱتَّخِذِي مِنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ بُيُوتاً﴾.
It is narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that he said: He inspired it.
The root meaning of «الوحي» in the language is making something known in a concealed way; this occurs through inspiration, through gesture, through writing and through hidden speech.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱسْلُكِي سُبُلَ رَبِّكِ ذُلُلاًً﴾.
Maʿmar and Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda that he said: obedient.
Abū Jaʿfar said: it is possible in the language that His saying ﴿ذُلُلاً﴾ refers to the paths, since one says «سبيلٌ ذلولٌ» and «سبُلُ ذُلُل», i.e. easy to travel.
And it is possible that it refers to the bees, i.e. they are submissive and made subservient.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِن بُطُونِهَا شَرَابٌ مُّخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوَانُهُ فِيهِ شِفَآءٌ لِلنَّاسِ﴾.
There are two views about it:
One of them: that the meaning is: in the Qurʾān there is healing for people.
This is a good view, i.e. in what We have related to you of signs and proofs there is healing for people.
It has also been said: in honey there is healing for people; and this view is also clear, because most of the drinks and electuaries with which people are treated have honey as their base.

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِِ﴾.
That is: he becomes decrepit until his intellect diminishes.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لِكَيْ لاَ يَعْلَمَ بَعْدَ عِلْمٍ شَيْئاً﴾.
That is: until he becomes ignorant again after knowledge; i.e. so that you may know that the One who returned him to this state is able to make him die and then bring him to life.

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ فَضَّلَ بَعْضَكُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ فِي ٱلْرِّزْقِ فَمَا ٱلَّذِينَ فُضِّلُواْ بِرَآدِّي رِزْقِهِمْ عَلَىٰ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ فَهُمْ فِيهِ سَوَآءٌ﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda that he said: this is a parable which Allah has struck, i.e. if one of you has a slave, he does not find it agreeable to give him of what he owns; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is more worthy of being declared above this.
The meaning of this view is that they took hold of Allah's provision and assigned a share of it to the idols and a share to Him. The meaning is: you are all human beings, and one of you has a slave, yet he does not give back to him anything of what he owns, nor make him his equal in it; so how can you take hold of Allah's provision and assign a share of it [to Him] and a share to the idols?
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَفَبِنِعْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ﴾.
That is: is it because Allah has bestowed blessings upon them that they deny the blessing and assign what He has provided them to someone other than Him?
It has also been said: the meaning is: is it because He has blessed them with clear explanation and proofs that they deny His blessings?
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: this parable is about Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and ʿĪsā, i.e. you do not do this with your slaves, so how can you be content for Me that I should take a human being as a son? Exalted is Allah, greatly exalted, above what they say.

nahhas-meani:72-72.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجاًً﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda concerning His saying ﴿وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجاً﴾ that he said: He created Ḥawwāʾ (Eve) from a rib of Ādam.
Someone else said: ﴿جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجاً﴾, i.e. from your own kind.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّنْ أَزْوَاجِكُم بَنِينَ وَحَفَدَةً﴾.
Sufyān al-Thawrī narrated from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that he said: «الحَفَدة» are the akhtān (in-laws).
Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated from [ʿĀṣim, from] Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, that he said: «الحَفَدة» are the aṣhār (relatives by marriage).
Shuʿba narrated from Zirr that he said: Ibn Masʿūd asked me about «الحَفَدة», and I said: they are the helpers. He said: they are the akhtān.
ʿAlqama and Abū al-Ḍuḥā said: «الحَفَدة» are the akhtān.
Ibrāhīm said: «الحَفَدة» are the aṣhār.
Abū Jaʿfar said: there is disagreement about the akhtān and the aṣhār. Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: the khatan is the husband and those who are of his kin, and the ṣihr is whoever is on the woman's side, such as her father, her paternal aunt and her maternal uncle.
Ibn al-Aʿrābī said the opposite of this concerning the akhtān and the aṣhār.
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: the khatan is whoever is on the woman's side, such as her father, her brother and the like, and the aṣhār are from both [sides] together; one says «أصْهَرَ فلانٌ إلى بني فلانٍ» and «صَاهَر» [i.e. he became related by marriage to them].
The saying of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, "they are the akhtān", can bear both meanings: it may be that he meant the woman's father and those of her relatives like him.
And it may be that he meant: and He has made for you from your wives sons and daughters whom you give in marriage, so that through them you have akhtān (sons-in-law).
Other things have been said about the verse.
ʿIkrima said: «الحَفَدة» are those of a man's children who benefit him.
Al-Ḥasan, Ṭāwūs and Mujāhid said: «الحَفَدة» are servants.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the root meaning of «الحَفَدة» in the language is service and work; one says «حفد يحفِدُ حَفْداً وحفوداً وحَفَداناً» when someone serves and works. From it is "وإليكَ نَسْعى ونَحْفِدُ" (and to You we strive and hasten in service), and from it is the saying of the poet:
حَفَدَ الوَلاَئِدُ حولَهُنَّ وأُسْلِمَتْ * بأكُفِّهِنَّ أَزِمَّةُ الأجْمَالِ
(The slave-girls bustled in service around them, and the reins of the camels were placed in their hands.)
The saying of whoever said "they are the servants" is good on this basis, except that according to Abū ʿUbayd it is then cut off from what precedes it, and a fronting and postponing (al-taqdīm wa-l-taʾkhīr) is intended by it, as if He had said: and He made for you ḥafada, i.e. servants, and made for you from your wives sons.

nahhas-meani:73-73.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لاَ يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ رِزْقاً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ شَيْئاًً﴾.
That is: they are not able to provide them with anything.

nahhas-meani:74-74.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ. فَلاَ تَضْرِبُواْ لِلَّهِ ٱلأَمْثَالََ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: do not worship besides Him what neither benefits you, nor harms you, nor provides for you.

nahhas-meani:75-75.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلاً عَبْداً مَّمْلُوكاً لاَّ يَقْدِرُ عَلَىٰ شَيْءٍ وَمَن رَّزَقْنَاهُ مِنَّا رِزْقاً حَسَناً فَهُوَ يُنْفِقُ مِنْهُ سِرّاً وَجَهْراً﴾.
This verse is difficult, and there are several views about it:
Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: this parable is about Allah, exalted be His mention, and those who are worshipped besides Him.
Qatāda said: this parable is about the believer and the disbeliever.
Qatāda holds that the owned slave is the disbeliever, because he gains no benefit in the Hereafter from any of his worship, and that the meaning of ﴿وَمَن رَّزَقْنَاهُ مِنَّا رِزْقاً حَسَناًً﴾ is the believer.
One of the lexicographers said: the first view is better, because it occurs between two statements about which we know of no disagreement among the exegetes — except those of them who deviate — that both are about Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; they are ﴿فَلاَ تَضْرِبُوا لِلَّهِ الأَمْثَالَ﴾ and after it ﴿وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلاً رَجُلَيْنِ أَحَدُهُما أَبْكَمُ لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ كلٌّ عَلَى مَوْلاَهُ﴾, meaning the idol, because it is a burden (kall) and a weight upon whoever keeps it.
And «المولى» is the guardian (al-walī).

nahhas-meani:76-76.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَوِي هُوَ وَمَن يَأْمُرُ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾.
He means Himself, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Qatāda said likewise: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commands us to justice, and He is on a straight path.
On this basis, the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلاً عَبْداً مَمْلُوْكاً﴾ is that He means by it what is worshipped besides Him, because it possesses neither harm nor benefit; and ﴿مَن رَزَقْنَاهُ مِنَّا رِزْقاً حَسَناً فَهُوَ يُنْفِقُ مِنْهُ سِرّاً وَجَهْراً﴾ refers to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, because He is the Generous One who provides for man from where he knows and from where he does not know.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās — and this is his wording as narrated from him — that he said: "This verse ﴿ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلاً عَبْداً مَمْلُوْكاً لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ﴾ was revealed concerning "Hishām ibn ʿAmr"; he is the one who spends from it secretly and openly, and his client (mawlā) was Abū al-Jawāb, who used to forbid him. And it has been said: it was revealed concerning two men: ﴿وَضَرَبَ اللهُ مَثَلاً رَّجُلَيْنِ﴾ — the dumb one of them, the burden upon his master, is "Usayd ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ", and the one who commands justice and is on a straight path is "ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān", Allah's mercy be upon him. ʿUthmān used to support his client; so ʿUthmān is the one who spends with justice and is on a straight path, and the other is the dumb one."
Al-Ḥasan said: ﴿عَبْداً مَمْلُوكاً﴾ is the idol.
The most fitting of the views on this is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās, narrated from him by Ḥammād ibn Salama, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās. Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, made clear that this verse was revealed about a particular slave who had no wealth — for it is not said of every slave (that he is not able to do anything). So it was revealed about him and about a master who had wealth from which he spent; and that the other verse was revealed about a particular man who had no wealth and was a burden upon his mawlā, i.e. his cousin or relative.
Allah struck these parables so that it be known that He is one God, and that nothing else should be likened to Him.
The saying of whoever said that it is an idol is not sound, because the name "slave" does not apply to an idol.

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ غَيْبُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
[That is: the knowledge of what in them is hidden from the servants.]
Then He said: ﴿وَمَآ أَمْرُ ٱلسَّاعَةِ إِلاَّ كَلَمْحِ ٱلْبَصَرِ أَوْ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ﴾.
Qatāda said: it is that He, Mighty and Majestic is He, says (كُنْ) "Be!", and that is like the twinkling of an eye, or nearer.
Someone else said: the meaning is: or it is nearer in your estimation; He did not mean that it is this near, but He meant to make His power known to us.

nahhas-meani:79-79.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ إِلَىٰ ٱلطَّيْرِ مُسَخَّرَاتٍ فِي جَوِّ ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾.
«الجوّ» is the distant air, and farther than it is «السُّكَاك»; the singular is «سُكَاكة».

nahhas-meani:80-80.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّن بُيُوتِكُمْ سَكَناًً﴾.
That is: a place in which you dwell.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّن جُلُودِ ٱلأَنْعَامِ بُيُوتاً﴾.
He means houses (tents) of leather and the like; and «الأنعام» are camels, cattle and sheep.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿تَسْتَخِفُّونَهَا يَوْمَ ظَعْنِكُمْ وَيَوْمَ إِقَامَتِكُمْ﴾.
That is: carrying them is light for you, in your travelling and your residing.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَمِنْ أَصْوَافِهَا وَأَوْبَارِهَا وَأَشْعَارِهَآ أَثَاثاً وَمَتَاعاً إِلَىٰ حِينٍ﴾.
Wool is from sheep, fur (awbār) from camels, and hair from goats.
Qatāda said: «الأثاث» is wealth.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «الأثاث» is wealth and adornment.
«الأثاث» according to the lexicographers is household goods such as furnishings and coverings; and «أثَّ يئِثُّ أثّاً» is said when someone has come to possess household goods. Abū Zayd said: the singular of «الأَثاث» is «أَثَاثَة».
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَمَتَاعاً إِلَىٰ حِينٍ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: until a term, and as sufficient provision (bulgha).

nahhas-meani:81-81.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّمَّا خَلَقَ ظِلاَلاً﴾.
He means the shade of trees; and Allah knows best.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ أَكْنَاناً﴾.
That is: what shelters you; the singular is «كِنّ».
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ سَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ ٱلْحَرَّ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda that he said: He means linen shirts.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَسَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُم بَأْسَكُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: He means coats of mail.
ʿUthmān ibn ʿAṭāʾ narrated from his father that he said: they were addressed only with what they knew. He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ أَكْنَاناً﴾, while what He made for them of the plains is more and greater, but they were people of mountains; ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ سَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ ٱلْحَرَّ﴾, while what protects from cold is more, but they were people of heat.
Al-Farrāʾ, "Yaḥyā ibn Ziyād", said: the meaning is: protecting you from heat and protecting you from cold; then it was omitted, as the poet said:
 فَمَا أَدْرِي إذَا يَمَّمتُّ وَجْهاً * أريدُ الخَيْرَ أيُّهُما يَلِيني
(I do not know, when I set out in some direction seeking good, which of the two will befall me.)
The meaning is: which of good and evil, because when he seeks good he guards against evil.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ يُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْلِمُونَ﴾.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās [that he read] ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَسْلَمُونَ﴾ and said: i.e. [safe] from wounds; but its chain is weak: ʿAbbād ibn al-ʿAwwām narrated it from Ḥanẓala, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
The apparent sense of the Qurʾān indicates Islam, because He enumerated the blessings and then said ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْلِمُونَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:82-82.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْبَلاَغُ ٱلْمُبِينُ. يَعْرِفُونَ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنكِرُونَهَا﴾.
Sufyān narrated from al-Suddī that he said: He means Muḥammad ﷺ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is good, and the meaning is: they know that the matter of the Prophet ﷺ is true, then they deny it.
Warqāʾ narrated from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, that he said: He means the dwellings, the livestock and what they are provided from them, and the garments of iron and clothing; Allah bestowed that upon them, but they did not give thanks, and they said: it belonged only to our forefathers and we inherited it from them.

nahhas-meani:84-84.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيداً﴾.
It is narrated that the prophet of every nation is a witness against it.

nahhas-meani:86-86.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَألْقَوْا إِلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَوْلَ إِنَّكُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾.
That is: their gods disowned them, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿سَيكْفُرونَ بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ وَيَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضِدَّاً﴾.
[Translator's note: the Arabic reads «جحدتم آلهتم», literally "their gods denied you"; rendered according to the evident sense.]

nahhas-meani:87-87.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَأَلْقَوْاْ إِلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلسَّلَمَ وَضَلَّ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُواْ يَفْتَرُونَ﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda that he said: they surrendered and were humbled; ﴿وَضَلَّ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُواْ يَفْتَرُونَ﴾, i.e. [what] they associated [with Him].

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَصَدُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ زِدْنَاهُمْ عَذَاباً فَوْقَ ٱلْعَذَابِِ﴾ [verse 88].
Masrūq narrated from ʿAbd Allāh that he said: they will be given in addition scorpions whose fangs are like tall palm trees.

nahhas-meani:89-89.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَابَ تِبْيَاناً لِّكُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾.
Abān ibn Thaʿlab narrated from Mujāhid that he said: an explanation of the lawful as distinct from the unlawful.

nahhas-meani:91-91.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلاَ تَنقُضُواْ ٱلأَيْمَانَ بَعْدَ تَوْكِيدِهَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means making the oath solemn.

nahhas-meani:92-92.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّتِي نَقَضَتْ غَزْلَهَا مِن بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ أَنكَاثاً تَتَّخِذُونَ أَيْمَانَكُمْ دَخَلاً بَيْنَكُمْ أَن تَكُونَ أُمَّةٌ هِيَ أَرْبَى مِنْ أُمَّةٍ﴾.
This is a difficult verse that requires reflection.
Qatāda said: «الدَّخَل» is treachery.
Someone else said: the meaning is: do not swear, or make oaths binding upon yourselves, and then break them, so that you would be like a woman who spun yarn, twisted it firmly and made it strong, then undid it.
«الأنكاث» is what is unravelled of silk, camel hair and the like, in order to be spun a second time; and from it one says «ناكث» (one who breaks [a pledge]).
It is narrated in the exegesis that a woman called Rabṭa bint Saʿd used to spin with a large spindle, and when she had twisted it firmly and perfected it, she would order her slave-girl and she would undo it.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said concerning His saying, the Exalted, ﴿أَن تَكُونَ أُمَّةٌ هِيَ أَرْبَى مِنْ أُمَّةٍ﴾: i.e. more numerous. He said: so they were commanded to fulfil the covenant, even if they [the others] were many.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid that he said: they used to make alliances with a people and make covenants with them, and when they learned that others were more numerous and stronger than them, they would break their covenant and ally themselves with the others; so Allah, exalted be His mention, forbade them that.
The meaning according to the lexicographers is: because a nation is, or on account of a nation being, more abundant than another nation, i.e. richer and more numerous. That is: do not make a covenant with a people and then, when they feel secure, break the covenant so that your associates may be richer and stronger.

nahhas-meani:97-97.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَنْ عَمِلَ صَالِحاً مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَيَاةً طَيِّبَةً وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْرَهُم بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونََ﴾.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: the good life is lawful provision; then he goes to Allah, and He rewards him according to the best of what he used to do.
It is also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās — al-Ḥakam narrated it from ʿIkrima from him — that he said: the good life is contentment.
Ibn Kathīr narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr concerning His saying, the Exalted, ﴿فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَيَاةً طَيِّبَةً﴾ that he said: in the Hereafter He will give him a good life.
ʿAwf narrated from al-Ḥasan: no one has a good life except in Paradise.

nahhas-meani:98-98.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَانِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ﴾.
The meaning is: when you intend to recite; this is as you say: "when you eat, say: In the name of Allah"; and similar to it in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَا أَيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إذَا قُمْتُمْ إلى الصَلاَةِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:100-100.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّمَا سُلْطَانُهُ عَلَىٰ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُ وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِهِ مُشْرِكُونَ﴾.
Ibn [Abī] Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid that he said: ﴿سُلْطَانُهُ﴾ is his argument; and he said: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِهِ مُشْرِكُونَ﴾: they make him equal to the Lord of the worlds.
[Translator's note: the text has «ابنُ نجيح»; elsewhere this narrator appears as Ibn Abī Najīḥ.]
Someone other than Mujāhid said: if the meaning were that they associated [others] with Satan, they would be believers; rather the meaning is: and those who, on account of him, are associators — as you say: "So-and-so became learned through you (بِكَ)", i.e. on account of you.

nahhas-meani:101-101.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا بَدَّلْنَآ آيَةً مَّكَانَ آيَةٍٍ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid that he said: We lifted it and put another in its place.
Someone else said: i.e. We abrogated a verse with a verse that is harder on them than it. ﴿قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُفْتَرٍ﴾, i.e. a liar. So He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنَّمَا يَفْتَرِي الكَذِبَ الَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. those who, when they see a sign which none but a prophet brings, deny it — these are the greatest liars of all.

nahhas-meani:103-103.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّمَا يُعَلِّمُهُ بَشَرٌ لِّسَانُ ٱلَّذِي يُلْحِدُونَ إِلَيْهِ أَعْجَمِيٌّ وَهَـٰذَا لِسَانٌ عَرَبِيٌّ مُّبِينٌ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from ʿIkrima, that he said: he was a slave-boy of the Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy, called — I think — Yaʿīsh.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that he said: he is "Salmān al-Fārisī", may Allah have mercy on him.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: he is "ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥaḍramī", and he was a Byzantine (Rūmī) who wrote well.
Abū ʿUbayd said: someone other than Mujāhid said: his name was "Jabr".
Abū Jaʿfar said: these views are not contradictory, because it is possible that they pointed to all of these and claimed that they were teaching him. The root meaning of «الإلحاد» in the language is inclining.

nahhas-meani:106-106.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَن كَفَرَ بِٱللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ إيمَانِهِ إِلاَّ مَنْ أُكْرِهَ وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ بِٱلإِيمَانِ﴾.
The exegetes [hold] that this verse was revealed concerning "ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir", may Allah have mercy on him, because he came close to some of what they urged him to do.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن مَّن شَرَحَ بِالْكُفْرِ صَدْراً فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is: whoever opened his breast to accept it.

nahhas-meani:110-110.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُواْ مِن بَعْدِ مَا فُتِنُواْ ثُمَّ جَاهَدُواْ وَصَبَرُواْ﴾.
All of this is about ʿAmmār; and the meaning is: and they were patient in jihād.

nahhas-meani:111-111.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ تَأْتِي كُلُّ نَفْسٍ تُجَادِلُ عَن نَّفْسِهَا﴾.
It is narrated that Kaʿb said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah have mercy on him: Hell will give a great roar on the Day of Resurrection, and there will remain no angel brought near nor prophet sent but that he falls to his knees, saying: "My Lord, myself!" — so much so that Ibrāhīm, the intimate friend of the All-Merciful, will fall to his knees and say: "I ask You only for myself." Then Kaʿb said: this is indeed in the Book of Allah, and he recited ﴿يَوْمَ تَأْتِي كُلُّ نَفْسٍ تُجَادِلُ عَن نَّفْسِهَا﴾.
Someone else said: this is indicated by ﴿يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ المَرْءُ مِن أَخِيهِ. وَأُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:112-112.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلاً قَرْيَةً كَانَتْ آمِنَةً مُّطْمَئِنَّةً﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda that he said: it is Mecca.
Someone else said: its people were in security and ease, then Allah tested them with killing and hunger for seven years. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿فَأَذَاقَهَا ٱللَّهُ لِبَاسَ ٱلْجُوعِ وَٱلْخَوْفِ﴾. The root meaning of tasting (al-dhawq) is with the mouth; then it came to be used for trial and testing.

nahhas-meani:115-115.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَنِ ٱضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ بَاغٍ وَلاَ عَادٍٍ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned it in Sūrat al-Baqara.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: whoever eats carrion while not compelled to it is a transgressor (bāghin) and one who exceeds the limit (ʿādin).
And it is narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid that they both said: if he makes the road unsafe and commits highway robbery, carrion is not made lawful for him. This is the meaning of what they said.

nahhas-meani:116-116.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَقُولُواْ لِمَا تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ ٱلْكَذِبَ هَـٰذَا حَلاَلٌ وَهَـٰذَا حَرَامٌٌ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the baḥāʾir and the suyyab [camels dedicated to the idols].

nahhas-meani:118-118.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعَلَىٰ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ حَرَّمْنَا مَا قَصَصْنَا عَلَيْكَ مِن قَبْلُ﴾.
Qatāda said: it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَعَلى الَّذِينَ هَادُوا حَرَّمْنَا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ﴾.

nahhas-meani:124-124.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّمَا جُعِلَ ٱلسَّبْتُ عَلَىٰ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱخْتَلَفُواْ فِيهِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Qatāda that he said: some of them made it lawful and some of them made it unlawful.
[Translator's note: the text reads «سعيدُ بن جُبَيرٍ عن قتادةَ»; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr was older than Qatāda, and the usual narrator from Qatāda in this book is Saʿīd (ibn Abī ʿArūba).]
Mujāhid said: they abandoned Friday and chose Saturday.

nahhas-meani:125-125.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱدْعُ إِلَىٰ سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَٱلْمَوْعِظَةِ ٱلْحَسَنَةِ وَجَادِلْهُم بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ﴾.
﴿وَجَادِلْهُم بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ﴾ — this is abrogated.

nahhas-meani:126-126.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُمْ فَعَاقِبُواْ بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبْتُمْ بِهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: when they mutilated Ḥamza, may Allah be pleased with him, they [the Muslims] said: we shall certainly mutilate them; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed this verse.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that he said: this verse was revealed before fighting [was prescribed], and before Sūrat Barāʾa.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is more fitting, and Zayd ibn Aslam said something similar.
He said: when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Medina, he was given permission to wage jihād against the polytheists and to be harsh with them.
What shows you that this was revealed in Mecca is His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَلاَ تَكُ في ضَيْقٍ مِمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ﴾; and most of their plotting, and his grief ﷺ over them, was in Mecca.
As for the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayra and Ibn ʿAbbās — "when Ḥamza was killed, Allah's mercy be upon him, the Prophet ﷺ said: I shall surely mutilate seventy of them", whereupon ﴿وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُمْ فَعَاقِبُواْ بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبْتُمْ بِهِ﴾ was revealed — the chains of both are weak.

nahhas-meani:128-128.t:
And His saying, exalted be His name: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَواْ وَّٱلَّذِينَ هُم مُّحْسِنُونََ﴾.
It is narrated from al-Ḥasan that he said: fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, in what He has forbidden you, and do well in performing His obligations.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَتَىٰ أَمْرُ ٱللَّهِ فَلاَ تَسْتَعْجِلُوهُُ﴾.
Some of them said: ﴿أَتَى﴾ ("has come") means "will come," because the meaning is known, so it becomes like your saying: "If you honour me, I honoured you" (i.e. I will honour you).
And it was said: Allah's informing in the past and in the future are one and the same, because it is known that it will happen, so it is in the position of what has already happened.
A third view — and it is the best of them — is that they considered far off the punishment Allah had promised them, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed them that it was near, saying: ﴿أَتَىٰ أَمْرُ ٱللَّهِ﴾,
i.e. in its nearness it is in the position of what has already come, as the Exalted said: ﴿إقْتَرَبَتِ السَّاعةُ﴾, and as one says: "The news has come to you," i.e. it has drawn near to you.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, the Qurʾān has come with the obligations, the rulings and the legal limits.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَاءِ مَآءً لَّكُم مَّنْهُ شَرَابٌ وَمِنْهُ شَجَرٌ فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ﴾.
Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ﴾ — in it you pasture (your herds).
Abū Jaʿfar said: And so it is in the language: one says أسَمتُ الإبلَ, i.e. I pastured them, so I am musīm, and they are musāma and sāʾima.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا ذَرَأَ لَكُمْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ مُخْتَلِفاً أَلْوَانُهُُ﴾.
Qatāda said: Of beasts, trees and fruits.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَرَى ٱلْفُلْكَ مَوَاخِرَ فِيهِِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Going and coming.
Al-makhr in the language is cleaving. One says مَخَرتِ السفينةُ تمخَرُ وتمخُرُ when the ship cleaves the water and you hear a sound from it, and that is when the winds blow. And makhr of the earth is only the water's cleaving it.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَلْقَىٰ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيََ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: That is, mountains.
Abū Jaʿfar said: One says رَسَا يرسُو when something is firm and stays fixed. Then the Exalted said: ﴿أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ﴾.
Ibrāhīm said: That is, lest it tip over.
Abū Jaʿfar said: One says ماد يميد when something moves and sways.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: I heard al-Ḥasan say: When Allah created the earth it was about to sway, so they (the angels) said: This will not keep anyone settled upon it. Then in the morning Allah had created the mountains, and the angels did not know from what the mountains had been created.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنْهَاراً وَسُبُلاً﴾.
That is, and He made in it rivers and ways.
Qatāda said: That is, roads.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعَلامَاتٍ وَبِٱلنَّجْمِ هُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, who said: Among the stars are landmarks, and among them are those by which one is guided.
Al-Farrāʾ said: (The star is) al-Jady (the Pole Star) and the two Farqads.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What the exegetes and the people of language hold, other than him, is that al-najm here means the stars.
Allah created the stars as an adornment for the heaven, as missiles against the devils, so that the number of years and reckoning may be known by them, and so that guidance may be found by them.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُنَزِّلُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةَ بِٱلْرُّوحِ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَآءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِِ﴾.
Hushaym narrated from Abū Bishr, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-Rūḥ is a creation among Allah's creations and a command among His commands; their forms are like the forms of the children of Ādam; no angel descends in the heaven but that one of them is with him.
And Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»] narrated from Mujāhid, who said: No angel descends but that a rūḥ is with him.
Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid said: I asked Abū Ṣāliḥ about al-rūḥ, and he said: They have forms like the forms of the children of Ādam, but they are not of them.
Al-Ḥasan said: The angels descend with al-rūḥ, i.e. with prophethood.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: "The angels descend with al-rūḥ" — he said: with revelation and mercy.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a good view, and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated it from Ibn ʿAbbās;
i.e. He sends them down with what is in the position of spirit and life, as the Exalted said: ﴿فَرَوْحٌ وَرَيْحَانٌ﴾.
And it was said: its meaning is mercy.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لاَ يَخْلُقُونَ شَيْئاً وَهُمْ يُخْلَقُونَ﴾.
Meaning the idols.
Muḥammad al-Yamānī read ﴿والذين يُدْعَوْنَ منْ دونِ اللَّهِ﴾ ("and those who are called upon besides Allah") with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the ʿayn.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْواتٌ غَيْرُ أَحْيَآءٍٍ﴾.
That is, they are dead, not living. ﴿وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: and the idols do not perceive.
And it is possible that the meaning is: and the polytheists do not perceive when they will be raised.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلأَنْعَامَ خَلَقَهَا لَكُمْ فِيهَا دِفْءٌ وَمَنَافِعُ وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونََ﴾.
Isrāʾīl narrated from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Offspring.
And Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»] narrated from Mujāhid, who said: al-dif' (warmth) is clothing that is woven, and the benefits are riding, milk and meat.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a good view, i.e. what gives warmth from their hair and other things. I reckon that Ibn ʿAbbās's position is that the benefits are the offspring, not the warmth; although al-Umawī narrated that al-dif' among the Arabs is the breeding of camels and the benefit derived from them, so this would be included in it.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا جَمَالٌ حِينَ تُرِيحُونَ وَحِينَ تَسْرَحُونََ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: When they come back in the evening, their humps at their largest from fatness and their udders full.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning according to the people of language is: and (when) you bring them back in the evening. One says أَرْحتُ الإبلَ when you bring them back from the pasture to the place where they stay at night; the place is called al-murāḥ, and in the ḥadīth: "If he steals it from the murāḥ, (his hand) is cut off."
And the meaning of ﴿تَسْرحُون﴾ is: you take them out in the morning to the pasture. سَرحْتُ الإبلَ أَسْرحُها سَرْحاً وسُروحاً — when you go out with them in the morning to the pasture and leave them to graze. And سَرَّحتُ هي [Translator's note: printed thus with ḍamma on the tāʾ; the sense "they went out to pasture" (سَرَّحَتْ هي) seems intended]: transitive and intransitive are the same.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَحْمِلُ أَثْقَالَكُمْ إِلَىٰ بَلَدٍ لَّمْ تَكُونُواْ بَالِغِيهِ إِلاَّ بِشِقِّ ٱلأَنفُسِِ﴾.
Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»] narrated from Mujāhid, who said: except with hardship.
Others said: the meaning is: were it not for the camels, you would not reach the lands except with hardship.
And it has been read ﴿إلاَّ بِشَقِّ الأَنْفُسِ﴾ (with fatḥa on the shīn), and it has the meaning of the first, except that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلْخَيْلَ وَٱلْبِغَالَ وَٱلْحَمِيرَ لِتَرْكَبُوهَا وَزِينَةًً﴾.
A group, among them ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, interpreted this as meaning that it is not lawful to eat these, because He said regarding camels ﴿وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ and did not say this regarding "horses, mules and donkeys."
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَخْلُقُ مَا لاَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
Its apparent sense is general, except that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muʿāwiya al-Qurashī narrated to us, saying: Mūsā ibn Muḥammad narrated to us from Ibn al-Suddī, from his father, regarding His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَيَخْلُقُ مَا لاَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — he said: the moth in clothes.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعَلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ قَصْدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, the making clear of guidance and misguidance.
Mujāhid said: That is, the path of truth. And this resembles ﴿قَالَ هَذَا صِرَاطٌ عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾,
i.e. according to My way and My religion. So too ﴿وَعَلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ قَصْدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾, i.e. the straight course among them is whatever is according to Allah's religion.
And it was said: it is the making clear of the truth, the proofs and the arguments.
And it was said: by "the way" here Islam is meant.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنْهَا جَآئِرٌ﴾.
That is, and among the ways there is one that is jāʾiz [Translator's note: so printed («جائز»), for «جائر»], i.e. deviating from the truth. Abū Bakr ibn Abī l-Azhar recited to me, saying: Bundār recited to me:
لَمَّا خَلَطْتُ دِمَاءَنَا بِدِمَائِهَا * ساَرَ الثِّفَالُ بهَا وجَارَ العَاذِلُ
(When I mingled our blood with hers, the slow beast went off with her, and the reproacher strayed.)
And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read ﴿ومنكُمْ جَائِرٌ﴾ ("and among you is one who deviates").
And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd likewise read this, by way of interpretation.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ لَهَدَاكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾.
That is, had He willed, He would have sent down a sign compelling you to believe; but He willed to reward and to punish.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِيَحْمِلُواْ أَوْزَارَهُمْ كَامِلَةً يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِِ﴾.
Al-wizr in the language is the heavy load, and sin is called wizr by way of likeness.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَمِنْ أَوْزَارِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: They are made to bear the sin of those whom they led astray, without anything being diminished from the sin of the one led astray.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَدْ مَكَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَأَتَى ٱللَّهُ بُنْيَانَهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْقَوَاعِدِ فَخَرَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلسَّقْفُ مِن فَوْقِهِمْ﴾.
Al-Aʿraj read ﴿السُّقُّفُ﴾ (plural, "the roofs").
Mujāhid said: By this He means "Nimrod son of Canaan," who disputed with Ibrāhīm about his Lord; and it is narrated that he built a great building, and it collapsed.
And it was said: This is a likeness, i.e. Allah destroyed them, so they were like one upon whom his building fell and who perished.
And it was said: Allah nullified their deeds, so they were like one upon whom his building fell.
The benefit of His saying, the Exalted, ﴿مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ﴾ is that one may say "such-and-such a house fell on me" when he owns it, even if it did not fall on him.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ يُخْزِيهِمْ وَيَقُولُ أَيْنَ شُرَكَآئِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تُشَاقُّونَ فِيهِمْ﴾.
The meaning is: Where are those whom you used to claim were My partners? i.e. Where are My partners according to your claim?! And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has no partner.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَلْقَوُاْ ٱلسَّلَمَ﴾.
That is, surrender; i.e. they yielded and surrendered.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلاَّ أَن تَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْمَلائِكَةُ﴾.
That is, to take their souls; ﴿أَوْ يَأْتِيَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ﴾, i.e. with the punishment [the earthquake and the swallowing up by the earth].

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُواْ لَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا عَبَدْنَا مِن دُونِهِ مِن شَيْءٍ نَّحْنُ وَلاۤ آبَاؤُنَا﴾.
[Some said: Allah censured these people who made their shirk a matter of His will.]
And some said: Whoever says this has disbelieved.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is an error in interpretation and is not accepted in exegesis; rather, they said this by way of mockery, as the people of Shuʿayb said to their prophet: ﴿إنَّكَ لأَنْتَ الحَلِيمُ الرَّشِيدُ﴾?, i.e. you are the forbearing, the right-minded, according to your own claim?
This is made clear by His saying: ﴿إنْ تَحْرِصْ عَلَى هُدَاهُمْ، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يَهْدِي مَنْ يُضِلُّ﴾. And in the reading of Ubayy: ﴿فإن اللَّهَ لا هادي لمن أضَلَّ اللَّهُ﴾ ("for Allah — there is no guide for whom Allah leads astray"), and it is a witness for those who read ﴿لا يُهْدَى﴾ (passive: "is not guided"), and it is the clear reading, as He said: ﴿وَمَا تَوْفِيقي إلاَّ باللَّهِ﴾.
And it is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he read ﴿لا يَهِدِّي مَنْ يَضِلُّ﴾ ("whoever goes astray is not guided"). The best of what has been said on this is what Abū ʿUbayd narrated from al-Farrāʾ: that one says هَدَى يَهْدي in the sense of اهتدى يهتدى ("to be guided"); the Exalted said: ﴿أَمَّنْ لاَ يَهْدِي إلاَّ أَنْ يُهْدَى﴾, meaning yahtadī.
Abū ʿUbayd said: We know of no one who narrated this other than al-Farrāʾ, and he is not suspect in what he reports.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It was reported to me from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd (al-Mubarrad) — as if the meaning of ﴿لا يَهْدِي مَنْ يُضِلُّ﴾ were: whoever He knows that of, and for whom that has been decreed beforehand in His knowledge. He said: «يَهْدي» does not mean yahtadī unless you say يَهَدِّي or يَهِدِّي.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلَّذِي يَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِِ﴾.
It admits two meanings:
One of them: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, indicated by the whole of the statement, the meaning being: rather, He will raise them, to make clear to them that wherein they differ.
The other view: that it is attached to His saying ﴿ولقَدْ بَعَثْنَا في كلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَسُولاً﴾, so the meaning is: and We have sent to every community a messenger, to make clear to them that wherein they differ, and so that those who disbelieve may know that they were liars.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُواْ فِي ٱللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُواْ﴾.
It is said that Bilāl and Ṣuhayb are meant by it; but what the whole of the statement requires is that it be general.
And it is narrated that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, when he handed the Emigrants their stipends, used to say to them: This is what Allah promised you in this world, and what He has stored up for you in the Hereafter is more. Then he would recite ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُواْ فِي ٱللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُواْ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَلأَجْرُ ٱلآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ﴾.
And Hushaym narrated from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, from al-Shaʿbī, regarding His saying ﴿لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً﴾ — he said: Medina.
Al-Ḥasan said likewise.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: By the good (ḥasana) He means victory and conquest; ﴿وَلأَجْرُ ٱلآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ﴾ — Paradise.
And Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»] narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً﴾ — he said: a good reputation (lisān ṣidq).

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ إِلاَّ رِجَالاً نُّوحِيۤ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾.
This was said to them because they said: ﴿أَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ بَشَرَاً رَسُولاَ﴾?
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿فَٱسْأَلُواْ أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ إِن كُنْتُم لاَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
It was said: He means the People of the Book, because they acknowledge that the messengers were of the children of Ādam.
Wakīʿ said: I asked Sufyān about His saying ﴿فَٱسْأَلُواْ أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ﴾, and he said: We have heard that they are those of the people of the Torah and the Gospel who embraced Islam.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿بِالبَيِّنَاتِ وَالزُّبُرِ﴾, i.e. with the proofs and the books.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُمْ فِي تَقَلُّبِهِمْ فَمَا هُم بِمُعْجِزِينَ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: In their journeys.
And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: By night and by day.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُمْ عَلَىٰ تَخَوُّفٍ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: I take one group and leave another group, so the remaining group fears that what befell its fellow will befall it.
And ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُمْ عَلَىٰ تَخَوُّفٍ﴾ — he said: by gradual diminution and tafarruʿ. [Translator's note: «تفرّع» is as printed; the sense is unclear, perhaps «تفزيع», "frightening," is meant.]
And Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»] narrated from Ibn Kathīr, from Mujāhid, who said: by diminution.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is the one known among the people of language. One says أخَذَهم على خَوْفٍ and على تخوُّفٍ when he diminishes them gradually, as Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid said.
The meaning of diminution is that He diminishes them in their wealth, their crops and their good, one thing after another, until He destroys them.
Al-Layth said: «على تخوُّف» — I have heard that it means "in haste."
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk's saying ﴿عَلَىٰ تَخَوُّفٍ﴾ means: He takes this town and leaves that one beside it, so that it becomes afraid.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَتَفَيَّأُ ظِلاَلُهُ عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَٱلْشَّمَآئِلِ سُجَّداً لِلَّهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: al-fayʾ is the shade.
Others said: al-tafayyuʾ is its returning from place to place, submissive and yielding; and such is the meaning of prostration.
Qatāda said: ﴿عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾ — in the morning; and His saying ﴿وَٱلْشَّمَآئِلِ﴾ — in the evening.
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَهُمْ دَاخِرُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, humbled.
